name: trading_fundamentals.json
description: Core trading vocabulary and concepts: instruments, orders, charts, indicator definitions and market mechanics. Reference material for the offline assistant; educational only.

terms.CFD: Contract for Difference. You speculate on price change without owning the asset; leveraged; can go long or short.
terms.Leverage: Borrowed exposure; controls a larger position with less margin. Magnifies gains and losses equally.
terms.Margin: Funds locked as collateral for an open leveraged position.
terms.Margin call / stop-out: Forced closing of positions when equity falls below the required level.
terms.Pip / Point / Tick: Smallest quoted price increment (definition depends on instrument).
terms.Lot / Volume: Trade size unit; value per point depends on broker and instrument.
terms.Spread: Difference between ask and bid; a cost paid on every round trip.
terms.Slippage: Difference between expected and actual fill price.
terms.Swap / Financing: Fee or credit for holding a leveraged position overnight.
terms.Stop-loss (SL): Order that closes a trade at a predefined loss.
terms.Take-profit (TP): Order that closes a trade at a predefined profit.
terms.Trailing stop: Stop that follows price at a set distance to lock in profit.
terms.R / R-multiple: Profit or loss measured in units of initial risk. Risk 10 and make 25 = +2.5R.
terms.Reward:Risk (RR): Distance to target divided by distance to stop.
terms.Win rate: Winning trades divided by total trades.
terms.Expectancy: Average profit per trade: win_rate*avg_win - loss_rate*avg_loss.
terms.Profit factor: Gross profit divided by gross loss.
terms.Volatility: Size/variability of price moves; often measured by standard deviation or ATR.
terms.ATR: Average True Range; average candle range including gaps over N periods (default 14).
terms.Trend: Sustained directional movement (higher highs and higher lows, or lower highs and lower lows).
terms.Range / Consolidation: Price oscillating between support and resistance.
terms.Support: Price zone where buyers have historically stepped in.
terms.Resistance: Price zone where sellers have historically stepped in.
terms.Breakout: Price closing beyond support or resistance.
terms.Retest: Price returning to a broken level to test it from the other side.
terms.Divergence (indicator): Price makes a new extreme but an oscillator such as RSI does not.
terms.Mean reversion: Tendency (or bet) that price returns to an average.
terms.Momentum: Rate of price change; persistence of direction.
terms.Regime: A distinct market state such as trending, ranging, high-volatility, low-volatility.
terms.Drift: Average directional tendency of price over time.
terms.Spike: Sudden large single-tick or few-tick move.
terms.Backtest: Applying rules to historical data to estimate performance.
terms.Forward test: Running rules on new data in real time (demo or tiny size) without changing them.
terms.Overfitting / Curve fitting: Tuning rules so tightly to past data that they fail on new data.
terms.Slippage + spread + fees: Total transaction cost that must be included in any test.
terms.Correlation: Statistic from -1 to +1 describing how two return series move together.
terms.Hedge: Offsetting position that reduces risk of another position.
terms.Counterparty: The other side of your trade; for synthetic CFDs on Deriv the broker.

items.name: Market order
items.description: Executes immediately at current price; subject to slippage.

items.name: Limit order
items.description: Buy below or sell above the current price at a specified level or better; may not fill.

items.name: Stop order (entry)
items.description: Buy above or sell below current price; used to enter breakouts.

items.name: Stop-loss
items.description: Protective exit at a loss limit.

items.name: Trailing stop
items.description: Stop that follows price by fixed distance.

items.name: OCO (one cancels other)
items.description: Pair of orders where filling one cancels the other, e.g. SL and TP.

concepts.name: Uptrend
concepts.rule: Sequence of higher highs (HH) and higher lows (HL). Broken when price makes a lower low that closes below the last HL.

concepts.name: Downtrend
concepts.rule: Sequence of lower highs (LH) and lower lows (LL). Broken when price closes above the last LH.

concepts.name: Range
concepts.rule: Repeated tests of a high and low without making new structure. Tradable by fading edges or breakout trading.

concepts.name: Swing high / swing low
concepts.rule: Candle whose high (low) is higher (lower) than N candles on each side (N commonly 2 to 5).

concepts.name: Change of character (CHoCH)
concepts.rule: First break of the most recent opposing swing point, hinting at a trend change.

concepts.name: Break of structure (BOS)
concepts.rule: Break of a swing point in the trend direction, confirming continuation.

concepts.name: Liquidity sweep
concepts.rule: Wick that takes out an obvious high/low and closes back inside; sometimes marks reversals.

concepts.name: Higher timeframe bias
concepts.rule: Trade in direction of the larger timeframe trend unless using explicit counter-trend rules.

patterns.name: Pin bar / hammer / shooting star
patterns.meaning: Long wick shows rejection of a price area.
patterns.use: Reversal or pullback-end signal at support/resistance or EMA.

patterns.name: Bullish/bearish engulfing
patterns.meaning: Candle body fully covers previous body.

topics.warning: Candlestick patterns have weak standalone predictive power; use with level, trend and risk rules. On RNG-driven synthetics they may carry no edge.

items.name: EMA
items.use: Trend and dynamic support/resistance; common N: 8, 20, 21, 50, 200.

items.name: RSI(14)
items.formula: RSI = 100 - 100/(1+RS), RS = avg gain / avg loss over N (Wilder smoothing).
items.use: Momentum; >70 overbought, <30 oversold in ranges; in strong trends RSI can stay extreme (range shifts to 40-80 in uptrends, 20-60 in downtrends).

items.name: MACD (12,26,9)
items.formula: MACD = EMA12-EMA26; signal = EMA9 of MACD; histogram = MACD-signal.

items.name: Bollinger Bands (20,2)
items.use: Volatility envelope; squeeze (narrow bands) then expansion; mean reversion in ranges, riding the band in trends.

items.name: ATR(14)
items.formula: TR = max(High-Low, |High-PrevClose|, |Low-PrevClose|); ATR = Wilder average of TR.
items.use: Stops and position sizing; stop = k*ATR.

items.name: Donchian channel(N)
items.formula: Highest high and lowest low of N periods.

items.name: VWAP
items.use: Intraday fair value on real markets; not meaningful on synthetics without real volume.

items.name: Z-score
items.use: Standardise spreads and returns for mean reversion.

guidance: Higher timeframe (H4/D1) = bias and levels; mid (H1/M15) = setup; lower (M5/M1) = entry timing.
Use a 4:1 to 6:1 ratio between timeframes (e.g. H4 -> H1 -> M15).
Lower timeframes have more noise and cost more as a percentage of each trade because spread is a larger share of the stop distance.
Only trade one primary timeframe pair at first.

table.signs: HH/HL or LH/LL, ADX>25, EMAs fanned and sloped
Flat EMAs, ADX<20, repeated reversals at same levels
table.approach: Mean reversion at edges, small targets; stop trading if range breaks

table.signs: Candles growing, ATR rising, breakout through level
Price repeatedly crosses EMAs with long wicks both sides

formulas.r_multiple: R = (exit - entry) / (entry - stop) for longs; reverse for shorts.
formulas.recovery_needed: recovery% = DD / (1 - DD)  (20% loss needs 25% gain; 50% loss needs 100% gain)
formulas.annualised_vol_from_tick: sigma_tick = stdev(log returns per tick); annual = sigma_tick * sqrt(ticks_per_year)

worked_examples.title: Position sizing
worked_examples.text: Equity 1000, risk 1% = 10. Stop distance 20 price units, 1 unit per price unit per lot. Size = 10/20 = 0.5 units. If stop hits you lose 10; if target at 2R hits you gain 20.

worked_examples.title: Breakeven win rate
worked_examples.text: With RR 1.5, BE win rate = 1/2.5 = 40%. Spread and fees push the real BE higher.

worked_examples.title: Drawdown math
worked_examples.text: After a 30% drawdown you need +42.9% to recover. Hence keep risk small.

items.name: CFDs (Deriv MT5 / cTrader)
items.traits: Long/short, leverage, no fixed expiry, spreads, swaps. Losses can exceed expectations if unmanaged.

items.name: Multipliers
items.traits: Leveraged with limited stake loss; stop-out when loss reaches stake; deal cancellation option may exist at a cost.

items.name: Accumulators
items.traits: Stake grows while price stays in a barrier range each tick; loses when barrier is hit.

items.name: Turbos / Vanillas / Rise-Fall
items.traits: Options-style, fixed stake risk, expiry or knock-out; payout structure must be understood.

topics.note: Check current product availability and terms on the Deriv site because they change by region.

research_context: Indicator effectiveness is market- and condition-dependent; recent studies find RSI more useful at extremes and MACD for momentum identification rather than universally predictive.
Any indicator claim should be re-validated per market and timeframe with out-of-sample data before being trusted.
